_why: Ratchet floors. A gate whose check count can fall silently cannot detect a deleted requirement: stripping four required headings from one pack made validate.py drop 1270->1269 and sloplint.py 224->223, both still green. Each number is the count measured on the commit named below. Raise freely; lowering one needs a reason in the same commit.
_measured_on: main after the T29 fix pass, 2026-08-14, twenty packs, clean tree with no nested worktree. Commit stamped in the follow-up that raises these.
_raised: validate_palette.py 1280 -> 1287 and sloplint.py 498 -> 504 on the T29 fix pass; validate.py holds at 2422. The palette rise is three new colour tokens (--terminal-dot, --mark-rest, --scrim) parsed in both theme blocks; the sloplint rise is the reduced-motion rule block the pack now ships as a fenced example, which is linted like a token layer. validate.py not moving is the informative one: twenty-six defects were fixed in this pass and the consistency gate's count did not change by one, because not a single one of them was structural. That is the shape of what a routing scenario buys and a gate cannot.
